column1: # Call-count fingerprint groups: NAME <TAB> PATTERN[|PATTERN...]
# One row per logical component. The patterns are plain SUBSTRINGS of a mangled symbol name,
# matched against both engines' callgrind profiles and summed per side; `|` separates
# alternatives, and a row normally carries one alternative per language because rustc and
# clang do not name the same function the same way. Each row is the claim "rfish calls this as
# many times as Stockfish does" -- a claim about the ALGORITHM, not about cost.
# A row whose pattern matches NOTHING on one side is a MISS and FAILS. A silent zero would
# read as agreement forever, which is precisely what an inlined-away symbol produces. If a
# compiler change inlines one of these, fix the row -- prefer a callee too big to inline over
# its caller -- and never delete the check.
# ROWS HAVE BEEN MOVED THAT WAY FIVE TIMES. The first two followed a refactor in this tree
# rather than a compiler change, and the weekly lane reported both as MISS on 2026-08-10:
#   do_move   `do_move_checked` became a one-line wrapper over `do_move_recording` when threat
#             recording landed, and the search calls the recording form DIRECTLY. The wrapper
#             inlines to nothing; the callee counts every make-move on every path and matches
#             upstream exactly (163345).
#   evaluate  `eval::evaluate` inlines into `SearchWorker::evaluate`, and that wrapper is
#             itself inlined at THREE of its six call sites -- it reports 35771 against
#             upstream's 62975, so a caller symbol cannot carry this row at all. The forward
#             pass every static evaluation runs can: `LayerStack::propagate` is 62975, and it
#             is a different symbol from the one `nnue_network` reads, so the two rows still
#             fail independently. Put the row back on the entry if rustc ever stops inlining
#             it -- an entry count is the claim this row would rather make.
# The third followed a refactor UPSTREAM, and moved the other side of `evaluate`:
#   evaluate  f740707f9 reduced `Eval::evaluate` to a network call and `scale_evaluation`,
#             and clang's PGO build now inlines it at every search call site, so the upstream
#             side matched nothing. `scale_evaluation` and `NetworkArchitecture::propagate`
#             inline too. The callee that survives is `Network::evaluate`, 41918 on both
#             sides at `bench 16 1 8`, and it is a different symbol from the
#             `AccumulatorStack::evaluate` that `nnue_network` reads upstream.
# The fourth followed a refactor in this tree again, and the weekly lane reported it as MISS
#   nnue_network  SFNNv17 took the PSQT head out of `Network::evaluate`, leaving a wrapper
#                 over `transform` and `propagate`, and rustc inlines it into
#                 `eval::evaluate`. The accumulator half survives:
#                 `FeatureTransformer::transform` runs once per evaluation, as upstream's
#                 `AccumulatorStack::evaluate` does, and it is a different symbol from the
#                 `propagate` that `evaluate` reads on this side.
# The fifth moved upstream's side of `evaluate` back the other way. The weekly lane reported
# it as MISS every week from 2026-10-19, the first run after the SFNNv18 sync:
#   evaluate  clang's PGO build now keeps `Eval::evaluate` as a call and inlines
#             `Network::evaluate` into it, the reverse of the third move. The entry is
#             entered once per static evaluation, 35714 times at `bench 16 1 8`, as rfish's
#             `LayerStack::propagate` is, and it is still a different symbol from
#             `AccumulatorStack::evaluate`. rfish's own entry cannot carry the row yet: it
#             counts 35666, so rustc still inlines it somewhere.
# The sixth moved UPSTREAM'S SIDE TO ANOTHER BUILD: the oracle's default, clang without a
# profile, in place of a PGO one.
#   evaluate      the reference inlines `Eval::evaluate` and keeps
#                 `NetworkArchitecture::propagate`, the same callee rfish's side already read.
#   do_move       it keeps the one-argument `Position::do_move` as a call, 130 of them, each
#                 reaching the form that does the work; the row names that form alone.
#   update_quiet  it inlines `update_quiet_histories`; `update_all` and `update_cont`, the
#                 caller and the callee, survive whole on both sides and replace it.
#   undo_move, gives_check, see_ge   were not gated, because PGO inlined them into upstream's
#                 search templates. The reference keeps them, so they are rows now.
# WHAT THIS IS FOR. Every other differential in this tree compares values: the bench anchor,
# the goldens, nnue-check, upstream-nodes. Each passes over a state divergence that happens
# not to move a number on the positions it drives. Two real defects were found by this and by
# nothing else, both in how a move is RENDERED for output:
#   * the PV reporter walked a cloned position, playing every PV move to name the next, and
#     truncated the line at the first move that failed a legality check. Upstream renders
#     against the root and prints the stored line whole.
#   * `bestmove ... ponder X` named the ponder move in the position AFTER the best move,
#     cloning and playing it first. Upstream names it against the root.
# Together, 1492 position clones and 1492 do_move/undo_move pairs per `bench 16 1 8` that
# upstream does not perform, and a PV that could come out shorter than upstream prints it.
# Every value gate was green through both.
movepick_next
search_node
qsearch
evaluate
nnue_network
update_all
update_cont
do_move
undo_move
gives_check
see_ge
legal
# NOT GATED: `update_quiet_histories`. Upstream's symbol reads 2217 against rfish's 26360 at
# `bench 16 1 8` because the reference inlines it at most of its call sites, so a row would
# assert that two compilers inline identically, which is not a fact about this port. Its
# callee carries the claim: `update_cont` is 40565 on both sides.
